pattern.crimePattern: fence silences a repairer who found stolen-phone parts
pattern.notes: Fictional repair shop; Luthuli Avenue is a setting only.

ob.reportedBy: Kelvin Njagi, apprentice, Signal Point electronics
ob.text: Apprentice Kelvin Njagi reports that repair technician Joel Mutiso (34) was found dead in the back room of Signal Point electronics repair, Luthuli Avenue, at 13:35, when Kelvin returned from lunch.

people.name: Joel Mutiso
people.bio: Could fix any radio on Luthuli Avenue with his eyes closed. Wrote every job in the job book in capitals.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 30s, magnifying loupe on a band pushed up on his forehead, grey work coat with pens in the pocket, focused gentle face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Wycliffe Barasa
people.bio: Brings radios in for repair more often than anyone on the street.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 20s, slim, fake-designer bomber jacket, two phones in hand, restless eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Simon Gakuru
people.bio: Owns the shop. He and Joel argued for months about Joel's share of the profits.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 50s, balding, short-sleeved shirt, phone pressed to his ear, irritated and shocked, ID-photo framing

people.name: Kelvin Njagi
people.bio: Learning the trade from Joel. Joel threatened last week to dismiss him for coming late.

image.brief: Kenyan teenager, 19, school-style haircut, oversized work coat, shocked and close to tears, ID-photo framing

people.name: Esther Njoki
people.bio: Her blue radio is still on the repair shelf.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 30s, long braids, a denim jacket, a woven market tote on her shoulder, puzzled and impatient, ID-photo framing

people.name: Aisha Noor
people.bio: Her counter faces the street and Signal Point's door.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 40s, a dark blue hijab neatly pinned, a long grey cardigan, reading glasses in one hand, alert and observant, ID-photo framing

people.name: Mama Wambui
people.bio: Serves githeri and tea to half the street. Statement by phone.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 50s, a kitchen apron over a printed dress, a patterned headscarf, a round cheerful face gone serious, ID-photo framing

locations.name: Signal Point electronics repair
locations.description: A narrow shop on Luthuli Avenue between a speaker seller and a phone-accessory shop. A front counter with the job book. A back room with a workbench, soldering irons, a heavy bench transformer, and a shelf of repaired items, each tied with a numbered paper tag.

hotspots.label: Back room, by the workbench
hotspots.text: Joel lies by the workbench. The report says he was struck from behind with the heavy bench transformer, which is on the floor.

hotspots.label: Repair shelf (zoom)
hotspots.text: The shelf opens in a zoom view. Tags dangle from items. On the rail, one tag is torn: only the stub is left, still tied on. Flip it.

hotspots.label: Job book on the counter
hotspots.text: Every repair: number, item, customer, notes. Joel's capitals.

hotspots.label: Under the workbench
hotspots.text: Something small and metal under the bench, among solder drips.

hotspots.label: Wall calendar
hotspots.text: A free calendar from a loans company, still on March.

image.brief: the cluttered back room of a Nairobi electronics repair shop, a workbench with soldering irons and gutted radios, a shelf of repaired radios and phones each with a numbered paper tag, a wall calendar, fluorescent tube light, no people

the concrete floor beside a cluttered electronics workbench, a heavy bench transformer lying on its side, chalk marks on the floor, scattered screws and a dropped soldering iron stand, police tape across the doorway behind, no body visible

body.label: A SIM tray from a smartphone. Not from any phone in the job book.

facts.text: Joel Mutiso was found dead in Signal Point's back room at 13:35.
Joel was struck from behind with the heavy bench transformer.
A torn tag stub, #318, is still tied to the shelf rail. The item is gone.
Job book: #318, red Philips radio, customer Wycliffe Barasa. Joel's note: 'CHECK INSIDE!!'
Job book: #317, blue Sony radio, Esther Njoki. Still on the shelf.
A loose smartphone SIM tray is under the workbench. It isn't from any job in the book.
Wall calendar: 'Mvua Holdings — Quick Loans · Title Searches — PesaPap Till 880 214'.
Aisha saw Joel alive in his doorway at 12:50.
At about 13:10 Aisha saw a young man leave Signal Point fast, carrying a red radio.
Aisha's sales book shows her serving customers at 13:00 and 13:08.
Aisha served Esther Njoki at 12:30; Esther left for work at Kenyatta Avenue.
Aisha: "Barasa? He's been in four times this month. Yes, that was him with the red radio at ten past one."
Simon's ticket: Nairobi–Mombasa, departed 21:00 last night. He's calling from Mombasa.
Mama Wambui: Kelvin ate githeri at her kibanda on Accra Road from 12:45 to 13:35.
Kelvin: the owner, Simon Gakuru, and Joel argued for months about Joel's share.
Kelvin: "I went for lunch at quarter to one at Mama Wambui's on Accra Road."
Kelvin admits Joel threatened to dismiss him last week for coming late.
Wycliffe: "I came for my radio, it wasn't ready, I left. He was fine."
Wycliffe: "I don't know anything about SIM trays."
Simon admits he and Joel argued about Joel's share. "We were going to agree. Now look."

interrogations.intro: Kelvin sits on an upturned crate outside, shaking. "I was only gone for lunch. Only lunch."

topics.reply: He shouted at me last week, said he'd dismiss me if I came late again. But he taught me everything. Everything.
Joel writes 'check inside' when something's wrong with a job. He never wrote it with two marks before.
Mr. Gakuru owns the shop. He and Joel argued about money for months. He went to Mombasa last night.
Mama Wambui on Accra Road. Githeri. She'll tell you.

interrogations.intro: Aisha closes her shutter halfway. "I saw. I saw a man running with a radio. I thought he was late for a matatu."

topics.reply: Barasa? He's been in four times this month. Yes, that was him with the red radio at ten past one. In a hurry.
Esther was here at half past twelve for a charger. Then she went back to her office on Kenyatta Avenue.

interrogations.intro: Simon, on speaker from Mombasa, over the sound of waves: "Joel? What do you mean, Joel?"

topics.reply: We argued about his share, yes. Every month. We were going to agree. I'll send you my bus ticket.
That one brings radios every week. I told Joel not to take his jobs. Something about him.

interrogations.intro: Wycliffe answers the number in the job book from a matatu. He agrees to come in. He doesn't bring a radio.

topics.reply: SIM trays? Every repair shop has a hundred.

interrogations.intro: Esther comes for her blue radio after work and finds the tape.

topics.reply: He fixed my radio for free last year because my son had exams. He was that kind of man.

prosecutor.pass: A torn tag, the job it belongs to, and the man seen carrying it away. That will hold.
fail: This doesn't hold up. Something was taken off that shelf. What, and whose was it?
No. Read the small writing. Then read the job book.

proof.concludes: The item torn off the shelf was job #318, a red radio belonging to Wycliffe Barasa.
The man who hurried out at 13:10, after Joel was last seen alive, was carrying a red radio.

eliminations.why: Simon took the 21:00 bus to Mombasa the night before.
Kelvin was eating githeri on Accra Road from 12:45 to 13:35.
Esther's radio is still on the shelf, and she was back at work on Kenyatta Avenue.
Aisha was serving customers in her own shop at 13:00 and 13:08.

reconstruction.text: For weeks Wycliffe has been bringing in radios to be 'fixed'. Inside them: SIM trays and chips for changing the identity numbers of stolen phones.
Wednesday morning. Joel opens job #318 and understands. He writes CHECK INSIDE!! in the job book and decides to go to the police.
About 13:05. Wycliffe comes for his radio. In the back room Joel tells him what he found. Wycliffe hits him from behind with the bench transformer.
He tears the red radio off the shelf, ripping its tag, and walks out at 13:10. A SIM tray falls out of the open radio and rolls under the bench.
On the wall, a free calendar from a loans company. Nobody looks at it. Yet.

tier1.line: Something is missing from the shelf. Every repair has a number. Flip the tag.

tier2.line: Job 318 was a red radio. Who did the neighbour see carrying a red radio?

ui.beatNotes: The shelf opens in a zoom view; tags can be flipped to read the number on the back. Teaches that small writing matters. The calendar is never highlighted.
